title: Breast cancer
text: resulting clusters visualised using plot_cluster_heatmaps(). breast cancer dataset, three distinct SCNA populations identified. Cluster 3 showed extensive inferred chromosome arm-level SCNA gains, including 1q, 8q 17q, recurrently gained breast cancer. Clusters 1 2 remained largely copy number neutral, Cluster 1 surrounding Cluster 3 regions Cluster 2 occupying distant tissue regions. Cluster assignments transferred back Xenium object using add_banksy_clusters(). Spatial cluster assignments visualised using plot_spatial_clusters(). Consistent inferred SCNA profiles, Cluster 3 predominantly localised tumour regions within tissue section, whereas Clusters 1 2 primarily associated surrounding tissue compartments.
code: # Plot cluster heatmap for lambda = 0.8 and resolution = 0.05 plot_cluster_heatmaps(     BANKSY.obj,     resolutions = c(0.05)     ) #> $res_0.05 # Add arm clusters of desired lambda and resolution back to main Xenium object xenium.obj <- add_banksy_clusters(xenium.obj,               BANKSY.obj,               resolution = 0.05) # Custom colour pallete col_pal_BANKSY <- c("#8CD17D","#F28E2B","#4E79A7")  # Plot spatial clusters plots <- plot_spatial_clusters(     xenium.obj,      cluster_palette = col_pal_BANKSY     )  # Plot one image with all spatial clusters plots$spatial_clusters_plot # Plot each spatial cluster separately plots$spatial_clusters_plot_facets

title: Quick start
text: SpatialCopyInference infers somatic copy number aberrations (SCNAs) directly Xenium spatial transcriptomics data. vignette demonstrates minimum SpatialCopyInference workflow compute SCNA-defined spatial clusters using human ovarian cancer dataset example. extended workflow also available SpatialCopyInference workflow. reproduce example, first download Xenium output files : https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/xenium-prime-ffpe-human-ovarian-cancer
code: # Path to Xenium output directory data_dir <- "path/to/Xenium_outputs/outs"  # Path to refined cell type annotations annotation_file <- "path/to/cell_type_annotations.csv" # Load SpatialCopyInference library(SpatialCopyInference)  # Import data xenium.obj <- import_xenium(data_dir, annotation_file)  # Quality control xenium.obj <- filter_cells(xenium.obj) xenium.obj <- filter_genes(xenium.obj, min_cells = 50, min_counts = 50)  # Normalisation xenium.obj <- normalise_data(xenium.obj)  # Compute chromosome arm means  arm_means <- compute_arm_means(xenium.obj, min_genes_per_arm = 5)  # SCNA inference arm_ratios <- compute_arm_ratios(arm_means,                                   xenium.obj,                                  group_var = "group",                                 reference = c("Fallopian Tube Epithelium", "Secretory Epithelial Cells"))  # Spatial clustering BANKSY.obj <- compute_spatial_clusters(arm_ratios = arm_ratios,           xenium.obj = xenium.obj,           lambda = 0.8,           resolution = 0.1) xenium.obj <- add_banksy_clusters(xenium.obj, BANKSY.obj)  # Visualisation plot_cluster_heatmaps(BANKSY.obj, resolutions = 0.1) #> $res_0.1 plot_spatial_clusters(xenium.obj) #> $spatial_clusters_plot #>  #> $spatial_clusters_plot_facets

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: SpatialCopyInference infers somatic copy number aberrations (SCNAs) directly Xenium spatial transcriptomics data. vignette demonstrates complete SpatialCopyInference workflow using human ovarian cancer dataset example. First, packages necessary vignette loaded.

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: workflow uses Xenium human ovarian cancer dataset 10x Genomics: FFPE Human Ovarian Cancer 5K Human Pan Tissue Pathways Panel plus 100 custom genes. Users wishing reproduce analysis first download Xenium output files : https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/xenium-prime-ffpe-human-ovarian-cancer Matched single-cell Gene Expression Flex data used cell type annotation: Human Ovarian Cancer FFPE Single Cell Gene Expression Flex. https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/17k-human-ovarian-cancer-scFFPE Cell type annotations generated using 10x Genomics label transfer workflow subsequently refined manual curation. https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/xenium-cell-type-annotation Xenium data accompanying cell type annotations imported using import_xenium(). function loads Xenium output files Seurat object optionally adds cell type annotations CSV file.
code: # Path to Xenium output directory data_dir <- "path/to/Xenium_outputs/outs"  # Path to refined cell type annotations annotation_file <- "path/to/cell_type_annotations.csv" # Import Xenium data xenium.obj <- import_xenium(data_dir, annotation_file)  # Dataset dimensions dim(xenium.obj) #> [1]   5101 407124  # Check if any unannotated cells sum(is.na(xenium.obj$group)) #> [1] 513

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Cell quality assessed using distributions detected genes (nFeature_Xenium) transcript counts (nCount_Xenium). Based distributions, low quality cells removed using filter_cells().
code: # Calculate quantiles for genes and counts probs <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75)  feature_quantiles <- data.frame(   quantile = names(quantile(xenium.obj$nFeature_Xenium, probs)),   features = as.numeric(quantile(xenium.obj$nFeature_Xenium, probs)) )  count_quantiles <- data.frame(   quantile = names(quantile(xenium.obj$nCount_Xenium, probs)),   counts = as.numeric(quantile(xenium.obj$nCount_Xenium, probs)) )  features_df <- data.frame(nFeature_Xenium = xenium.obj$nFeature_Xenium) counts_df <- data.frame(nCount_Xenium = xenium.obj$nCount_Xenium)  # Plot distribution info on top of Violin plots using ggplot2 # add + 1 to counts for log scale visualisation Vln_features <- ggplot(features_df, aes(x = "", y = nFeature_Xenium + 1)) +                           geom_violin(fill = "salmon", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +                           geom_boxplot(width = 0.08, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +                           geom_hline(yintercept = feature_quantiles$features + 1,                                       linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +                           geom_text(data = feature_quantiles,                                      aes(x = Inf, y = features + 1,label = paste0(quantile, "(",features + 1,")")),                                      inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +                           scale_y_log10() +                           annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +                           labs(y = "nFeature_Xenium + 1", x = NULL, title = "nFeature_Xenium")+                           theme_classic()   Vln_counts <- ggplot(counts_df, aes(x = "", y = nCount_Xenium + 1)) +                         geom_violin(fill = "salmon", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +                         geom_boxplot(width = 0.08, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +                         geom_hline(yintercept = count_quantiles$counts + 1,                                    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +                         geom_text(data = count_quantiles,                                    aes(x = Inf, y = counts + 1,label = paste0(quantile, "(",counts + 1,")")),                                    inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +                         scale_y_log10() +                         annotation_logticks(sides = "l") +                         labs(y = "nCount_Xenium + 1", x = NULL, title = "nCount_Xenium")+                         theme_classic()   print(Vln_features | Vln_counts) # Dataset dimensions before filtering dim(xenium.obj) #> [1]   5101 407124  # Filter low quality cells xenium.obj <- filter_cells(xenium.obj)  # Dataset dimensions after filtering dim(xenium.obj) #> [1]   5101 398993

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: package includes pre-computed hg38 positional information genes, chromosomes chromosome arms. resources generated using get_genomic_info() create_hg38_annotation() can regenerated required. hg38_gene_info contains gene level positional information, hg38_chrom_info contains chromosome centromere coordinates used throughout SpatialCopyInference analyses.

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Chromosome arm means cell computed using compute_arm_means(), aggregates gene expression values within chromosome arm calculates mean expression. summarises expression chromosome arm level, basis subsequent copy number inference. minimum number genes required per chromosome arm can specified.

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Reference profiles used somatic copy number inference computed using compute_reference(). Reference profiles can generated cells, multiple selected cell populations combined individual cell populations. ovarian cancer dataset, compare default reference generated cells reference derived normal epithelial populations Fallopian Tube Epithelium Secretory Epithelial Cells, include cell types origin thought give rise high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). Normal diploid reference populations preferred less likely harbour SCNAs therefore provide stable baseline copy number inference. suitable diploid reference population unavailable, global mean across cells can used instead. detailed comparison chromosome arm mean expression profiles across annotated cell populations available companion website Cell type means. reference profiles compared alongside representative normal tumour cell populations.
code: # Global reference (default) global_ref_arm_means <- compute_reference(   xenium.obj   )  global_ref_arm_means$group <- "All Cells"  # Combined epithelial reference epithelium_ref_arm_means <- compute_reference(   xenium.obj,   group_var = "group",   group_names = c("Fallopian Tube Epithelium", "Secretory Epithelial Cells")   )  epithelium_ref_arm_means$group <- "Epithelium"  # Fallopian Tube Epithelium ft_ref_arm_means <- compute_reference(   xenium.obj,   group_var = "group",   group_names = "Fallopian Tube Epithelium")  ft_ref_arm_means$group <- "Fallopian Tube Epithelium"  # Secretory Epithelial Cells secretory_ref_arm_means <- compute_reference(   xenium.obj,   group_var = "group",   group_names = "Secretory Epithelial Cells")  secretory_ref_arm_means$group <- "Secretory Epithelial Cells"  # Proliferative Tumour Cells (comparison only) tumour_ref_arm_means <- compute_reference(   xenium.obj,   group_var = "group",   group_names = "Proliferative Tumour Cells")  tumour_ref_arm_means$group <- "Proliferative Tumour Cells" arm_means_to_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(   global_ref_arm_means,   epithelium_ref_arm_means,   ft_ref_arm_means,   secretory_ref_arm_means,   tumour_ref_arm_means)  # Plot profiles ggplot() +   geom_vline(     xintercept = hg38_chrom_info$cum_centromere_mid,     linetype = "dashed",     linewidth = 0.3   ) +   geom_vline(     xintercept = hg38_chrom_info$cum_length,     linewidth = 0.3   ) +   geom_segment(     data = dplyr::filter(       arm_means_to_plot,       arm == "p"     ),     aes(       x = p_start,       xend = p_end,       y = mean_arm_expr,       colour = group     ),     linewidth = 0.8,     linetype = "11"   ) +   geom_segment(     data = dplyr::filter(       arm_means_to_plot,       arm == "q"     ),     aes(       x = q_start,       xend = q_end,       y = mean_arm_expr,       colour = group     ),     linewidth = 0.8,     linetype = "11"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c(       "Proliferative Tumour Cells" = "#F1CE63",       "Epithelium" = "purple",       "Fallopian Tube Epithelium" = "#59A14F",       "Secretory Epithelial Cells" = "#F28E2B",       "All Cells" = "black"     )   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = hg38_chrom_info$cum_chromosome_mid,     labels = hg38_chrom_info$chrom,     expand = c(0, 0)   ) +   theme_classic() +   theme(     axis.text.x = element_text(       colour = "black",       size = 8,       angle = 50,       hjust = 1     ),     axis.text.y = element_text(       colour = "black",       size = 9     ),     axis.title.x = element_text(       colour = "black",       size = 8     ),     axis.title.y = element_text(       colour = "black",       size = 8     ),     legend.text = element_text(       colour = "black",       size = 8     ),     legend.position = "right",     legend.title = element_blank()   ) +   ylim(0, 1) +   labs(     x = "Chromosome",     y = "Log-normalised expression",     title = "Reference comparison"   )

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Somatic copy number inference performed comparing chromosome arm mean expression levels chosen reference profile. , chromosome arm log ratios computed using epithelial reference compute_arm_ratios(). example, epithelial reference defined combination Fallopian Tube Epithelium Secretory Epithelial Cells cell populations specified via reference argument.

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Spatial clustering performed incorporate spatial context SCNA inference, based assumption neighbouring cells likely share common evolutionary trajectories. Spatial clustering implemented using BANKSY*, integrates neighbourhood composition local spatial structure identify spatially coherent cell populations: *Singhal, V., Chou, N., Lee, J. et al. BANKSY unifies cell typing tissue domain segmentation scalable spatial omics data analysis. Nat Genet 56, 431–441 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-024-01664-3 , BANKSY applied chromosome arm log ratio profiles generated compute_arm_ratios() using compute_spatial_clusters(). parameter lambda controls contribution spatial information, resolution controls cluster granularity. Optimal values dataset dependent may require tuning user. detailed comparison clustering parameters ovarian cancer dataset available companion website Cluster parameter optimisation.
code: # BANKSY clustering using lambda = 0.8 BANKSY.obj <- compute_spatial_clusters(           arm_ratios = arm_ratios,           xenium.obj = xenium.obj,           lambda = 0.8,           resolution = c(0.1)           )

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: resulting clusters can visualised using plot_cluster_heatmaps(). Multiple resolutions can evaluated simultaneously optimising clustering parameters. ovarian cancer dataset, identified clusters exhibit distinct chromosome arm-level SCNA profiles, resolving tumour, non-malignant intermediate populations. Validation inferred chromosome arm level SCNAs, including recurrent chr3q chr8q gains, SCNAs observed TCGA Ovarian Serous Cystadenocarcinoma available companion website TCGA. Cluster assignments can transferred back Xenium object using add_banksy_clusters(). Spatial cluster assignments can visualised using plot_spatial_clusters().  composition cell groups across BANKSY-derived spatial clusters visualised using plot_cluster_composition(). cell group, proportion cells assigned spatial cluster displayed stacked bar plot. Cell groups ordered dominant spatial cluster facilitate comparison cluster composition patterns.
code: # Plot cluster heatmap for lambda = 0.8 and resolution = 0.1 heatmap <- plot_cluster_heatmaps(             BANKSY.obj,             resolutions = c(0.1)             ) heatmap$res_0.1 # Add arm clusters of desired lambda and resolution back to main Xenium object xenium.obj <- add_banksy_clusters(xenium.obj,               BANKSY.obj,               resolution = 0.1) # Custom colour pallete col_pal_BANKSY <- c("1"="#8CD17D","2"="#F28E2B","3"="#4E79A7","4"="#F1CE63")  # Plot spatial clusters plots <- plot_spatial_clusters(     xenium.obj,      cluster_palette = col_pal_BANKSY     )  # Plot one image with all spatial clusters plots$spatial_clusters_plot # Plot each spatial cluster separately plots$spatial_clusters_plot_facets # Custom colour palette col_pal_BANKSY <- c("#8CD17D","#F28E2B","#4E79A7","#F1CE63")  # Plot cluster composition with custom palette plot_cluster_composition(xenium.obj,     cluster_palette = col_pal_BANKSY     )

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Differential expression analyses identify genes associated distinct SCNA-defined cell populations across spatial clusters using compare_spatial_clusters(). function performs differential expression testing Gene Ontology enrichment analysis selected spatial clusters. Genes filtered using log-fold change adjusted p-value thresholds identify - downregulated markers. Functional enrichment analyses significantly upregulated genes reveal biological processes associated spatial cluster. , Cluster 1 (tumour-associated) Cluster 2 (non-malignant) compared example.
code: # Compare Cluster 1 vs 2 cluster1v2 <- compare_spatial_clusters(               xenium.obj,               ident_1 = "1",               ident_2 = "2")  # Differentially expressed genes head(cluster1v2$de) #>         p_val avg_log2FC pct.1 pct.2 p_val_adj #> H19         0  3.6709337 0.888 0.111         0 #> CD47        0  3.1226967 0.800 0.049         0 #> LAPTM4B     0  3.3033381 0.779 0.032         0 #> YWHAZ       0  1.2678262 0.752 0.083         0 #> NORAD       0  0.8549308 0.766 0.109         0 #> HNRNPD      0  0.7824252 0.782 0.126         0  # GO enrichment dot plot  cluster1v2$go_dotplot # GO enrichment cnet plot cluster1v2$go_cnetplot

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Differentially expressed genes mapped across genome using plot_gene_density(). Rather randomly distributed, differentially expressed genes cluster within specific genomic regions form local hotspots associated underlying inferred SCNAs. Visualising hotspots facilitates identification candidate driver genes genomic regions may contribute cancer progression.
code: # Custom driver genes driver_genes <- c("MYC", "PIK3CA", "CCNE1", "KRAS",                    "TERT","AKT1", "AKT2", "AKT3", "CCND1",                    "CCND2", "CCND3", "KRAS", "MECOM")  # Plot gene density plot_gene_density_obj <- plot_gene_density(     de_results = cluster1v2$de,     driver_genes = driver_genes,     raised_driver_genes = c("MECOM","AKT2") )

title: SpatialCopyInference workflow
text: Differentially expressed genes grouped local genomic clusters using identify_gene_clusters(). Genes located within 2 Mb one another assigned cluster. plot_gene_clusters() visualises genomic distribution clusters can highlight known driver genes within clustered regions. facilitates interpretation genomic regions underlying cluster-specific transcriptional programmes. ovarian cancer dataset, several largest gene clusters occur within chromosome arms showing recurrent gains tumour population overlap established HGSOC driver genes, including MECOM, PIK3CA, MYC CCND1.  Chromosome-level visualisations generated using plot_gene_clusters_by_chromosome(). Individual chromosomes can explored greater detail, optional overlays genomic density signals driver gene annotations. Chromosome 3 shown example .
code: gene_clusters <- identify_gene_clusters(     de_results = cluster1v2$de) # Plot gene clusters plot_gene_clusters(gene_clusters = gene_clusters,           driver_genes = driver_genes,           raised_driver_genes = c("MECOM","AKT2")           ) # Plot gene clusters chromosome 3 plot_gene_clusters_by_chromosome(     gene_clusters = gene_clusters,     chromosome = "chr3",     density = plot_gene_density_obj$signal_gr,     driver_genes = driver_genes,     raised_driver_genes = c("MECOM", "AKT2")     )

title: Spatial Copy Number Inference from Xenium Data
text: SpatialCopyInference infers chromosome arm-level somatic copy number aberrations (SCNAs) directly Xenium spatial transcriptomics data. package identifies spatially maps SCNA-defined cell populations spatial clustering provides downstream tools visualisation, differential expression analysis, pathway enrichment identification genes genomic regions associated inferred SCNAs. SpatialCopyInference enables study tumour evolution early cancer development situ. Documentation, including entire workflow using human ovarian cancer dataset, available . can read SpatialCopyInference preprint.

title: Spatial Copy Number Inference from Xenium Data
text: minimum workflow shown :
code: # Import data xenium.obj <- import_xenium(data_dir, annotation_file)  # Quality control xenium.obj <- filter_cells(xenium.obj) xenium.obj <- filter_genes(xenium.obj)  # Normalisation xenium.obj <- normalise_data(xenium.obj)  # SCNA inference arm_means <- compute_arm_means(xenium.obj) arm_ratios <- compute_arm_ratios(arm_means, xenium.obj)  # Spatial clustering BANKSY.obj <- compute_spatial_clusters(arm_ratios, xenium.obj)  xenium.obj <- add_banksy_clusters(xenium.obj, BANKSY.obj)  # Visualisation plot_cluster_heatmaps(BANKSY.obj) plot_spatial_clusters(xenium.obj)  # Downstream analyses cluster_results <- compare_spatial_clusters(xenium.obj, ident_1 = "1", ident_2 = "2") plot_gene_density(de_results = cluster_results$de) gene_clusters <- identify_gene_clusters(de_results = cluster_results$de) plot_gene_clusters(gene_clusters = gene_clusters)
